Cindervale Idle · design proposal · measured against build 0.9.127.3 · nothing here is in the game

Magic chooses how it hurts

Melee and Ranged hit with whatever they are holding. A mage picks one of four elements for the fight, and how big a spell to cast with it: sixteen spells, Fire Bolt to Shadow Surge. Each element does a different job, every monster is weak to one of them, and a bigger spell spends more runes and hits harder. That is the whole proposal. The rest of this page is what it takes to make it true in every place the game reads a weapon, a damage stat or a combat level.

The design was built as a working prototype laid over build 0.9.127.3 without editing it, and a simulator asked the game's own functions for every number below: 52 checks, 0 failing. The mock-ups in section 11 are that prototype photographed in the real game. Anything that was not simulated says provisional.

Third draft. What changed since the first.

The spell bar. You said the spell has to be easy to pick in combat. It is now eight buttons under your own health bar, four sizes and four elements, each about 46 px tall, and they work while the fight runs: press one and it applies from your next cast. Section 11 has it in a fight, mid-switch and in a raid. Question 7 has the one thing that leaves open.

Spells come in four sizes. You asked for more than four spells: each element now has a Bolt, a Blast, a Wave and a Surge, which spend one to four runes a cast and hit harder as they grow. Section 04 opens with them, section 11 has the buttons, and question 17 is the call.

A batch of runes is bigger, and a correction. The first draft read a finished mage's rune bill at Agility 1. A finished mage has Agility 99 and casts a third more often, which put the bill a third higher than I said and the staff just under the band. A batch is now 40 runes for each rune the biggest spell spends (it was 25), every rune table is read at the Agility the character would have, and the real-monster fights are run at the fighter's own Agility. The weapon maths, the best in slot table and the Spire wall did not move.

One rename. The fast Magic style was called Surge. It is Swift now, because Surge is a spell.

00

What is there today

Checked against cindervale.html at build 0.9.127.3, not against notes.
The stub
Magic is a label, an icon and a tile that says Soon.COMBAT_STAT_NAME has the word, a painted magic stat icon is in the item art, and COMBAT_LOADOUTS has a tile flagged soon that the Presets tab draws. state.combatXp has no magic key and COMBAT_STATS has no entry.
Dead markup
The locked Magic pill in the combat panel never reaches the screen.renderCombat still builds it (baseStatPill, with Ranged locked beside it) into statsBlock, which becomes statsCard, which nothing places (the name appears once in the file, where it is declared). The live readout is the one line under the Training buttons that says Ranged and "equip a bow to train it".
Damage types
All 57 monsters are weak to slash, stab or crush. None is weak to a bow.DMG_TYPES is slash, stab, crush, ranged. 57 of 57 monsters have a melee weakness and 27 resist a melee type. The four weakTo:'ranged' rows are the Aerie birds, behind AERIE_LIVE, so in the live game a sword with the right edge gets +15% everywhere and a bow gets it nowhere. The 27 raid stages and nine Spire monsters follow the same three types.
Enchanting
One enchant on tier 8 gear costs 200 Arcane Dust, 80 Rune Fragments and 50 Mana Essence.A maxed character makes about 464 Arcane Dust an hour in Alchemy, brews 381 Mana Essence, and finds 6.7 Rune Fragments an hour (Mine starsteel 2.2%). Fragments are the scarce one: a single tier 8 enchant is about twelve hours of mining. Section 09 shows what Magic takes from this pool, which is nothing a player would notice.
No sink
Thirteen materials are used by nothing.The audit lists them by name: Runed Bone, Drakeforged Rune, Riftshard and Barrow Dust from the raids, charcoal from every fire past Firemaking 12, Energy Crystal, Stamina Shard, Ember Resin, Golden Spore, Abyssal Scale, Void Essence, Goblin Ear and Splintered Club. Magic gives four of them a use, and gives Spider Silk, which one Alchemy poultice uses today, something to be farmed for.
Armour
There is no cloth to fight in.Plate is Crafting on bars, leather is Crafting on hides and carries the light flag that makes it the ranged line. The crafted ladder is seven tiers, with three raid tiers above it for both.
Combat Mastery
The key magic is Warfare, and the board is exactly full.Onslaught, Marksman, Bulwark and Warfare are 30 points each, with three 4 point bridges: 132. A finished character can earn exactly 132 (98 levels, 4 milestones, 9 bosses, 12 zones, 4 raids, 5 Spire floors), and the audit asserts the two numbers match. A fifth column has to bring its own points.
Ranged gaps
Five things Ranged shipped without, which Magic would inherit.Offline combat spends no arrows: offlineCombatResolve has no ammunition in it at all. The arena has no quiver readout: the first sign a quiver is empty is the fight stopping. The save slot shows the wrong combat level for an archer: mmSummary still averages the four melee stats. A Hawkeye Draught shows nothing in the effects bar. A guild quest cannot ask for a Ranged level: gdReqMet knows only the four melee stat names. Each is the same function Magic has to touch, so each is cheaper fixed for both at once.
Notes that drifted
CLAUDE.md still calls Ranged a placeholder.Also measured in this session: 544 acts and 76 families (the notes say 542 and 75), 570 tree node and state pairs (480), 1,268 audit assertions (1,255), and skilling tools run to tier 6.
01

The one decision that makes it not Ranged

Three candidates. One pick. What the pick costs.
Candidate A · kept as the cost

Every cast spends runes

True, and it stays. But it is the sentence Ranged already owns. A rune that is an arrow with a glow on it is a new recipe list and no new game.

So runes are the price of Magic, not what Magic is.

Candidate B · the pick

A mage chooses how it hurts

Four elements, one button each: Fire, Frost, Storm, Shadow. A sword's damage type is the sword. A bow has none. A mage changes it between fights without touching gear.

And four sizes of each: Bolt, Blast, Wave, Surge. A bigger spell spends more runes and hits harder, so the rune stack is a second thing a mage decides how to spend.

Every monster is weak to one element and most resist one, for the same 15% a melee weakness is worth. Each element also does one small job of its own: Fire burns, Frost slows the monster, Storm cannot miss, Shadow heals you.

Candidate C · rejected

A spell grows the longer the fight runs

Weak on trash, strong on bosses. It gives Magic a place, but no single number can then say whether it is balanced, and the Spire's own sword already does it (Sunder stacks).

Worth one Mastery node at most, not the whole style.

What the pick costs

Data
An element pass over every monster.57 monsters, 27 raid stages and 9 Spire monsters each get a weak element and most get a resisted one. Two new fields, weakEl and resistEl, so the melee fields are untouched. Section 04 has all of them.
Screen
One new bar on the arena.Eight buttons under your own health bar: four spell sizes, then four elements. They are the only new controls a player has to learn, they are the widest buttons in the arena after Engage, and they work while the fight runs. Section 11 has the measurements.
Idle risk
The wrong element is a real mistake.Parked on a resisted element you do 85% where the right one does 115%, a quarter of your damage. So the button says "resists -15%" on the monster in front of you, and the Monster Log and the monster card say it before you start.
Balance
Four small effects that must not become the reason to play.Measured on real monsters: Fire is worth 0.8 to 2.4% more damage, Storm 1.0 to 2.0%, Frost 5.8 to 10.1% less damage taken, Shadow heals back 3.2 to 7.1% of the damage you take. The weakness is the big number on purpose.
No new plumbing
Every element reuses an effect the fight already has.Fire is foeStatus.burn, Frost is the slow Pinning Shot applies, Storm is the roll Plummet and Windcutter use, Shadow is the lifesteal line. No new timer, status or damage path.
02

The skill

One stat, like Ranged. No save moves.
ProposalWhy
Statstate.combatXp.magic, level 1 to 99 on XP_CUMThe sixth combat stat. It does the job of Attack and Strength for a staff or a wand, exactly as Ranged does for a bow.
XPcombatXpStat() returns magic while a staff or wand is heldAll seven places that ask which stat is being trained already call that function. Hitpoints keeps its share.
WeaponsStaves and wands need Magic, on COMBAT_GEAR_REQ: 1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 55, 70, 80, 90, 99, 99The same ladder a blade climbs on Attack and a bow on Ranged. One line in combatGearReq.
RobesNeed Defence, like all armourOne rule for everything you wear. The Warded style trains it. This is question 3 in section 17.
Combat levelfloor(( max(attack + strength, ranged × 2, magic × 2) + defence + hitpoints ) / 4)One more term inside the max that Ranged added. With Magic at 1 the term is 2, and attack + strength is never less.
Checked: no existing save changes combat level. measured

200,864 saves were put through the old formula and the new one: every corner (Magic missing from the save, Magic at 0 XP, Magic at level 1, against Attack, Strength, Ranged, Defence and Hitpoints at 1, 2, 50 and 99) and 200,000 random ones. 0 moved. A pure mage reaches 99, a pure archer 99 and a pure fighter 99.

How the numbers were chosen.

The biggest spell a rune powers gets the arrow's strength, tier for tier, and a wand is exactly as accurate as the sword and the shortbow. That makes a wand a shortbow that casts 2% slower (cast speed ×0.87 against ×0.85), and the burn from Fire gives the 2 to 3% back on a long fight. Pegging Magic to the bows is deliberate: theirs is the ladder that harness has already tuned, so Magic inherits the tuning at every tier and not only at the four that were tested.

04

Spells and elements

Sixteen spells: four elements, four sizes of each.

Sixteen spells. Each element comes in four sizes: Bolt, Blast, Wave and Surge. A bigger spell spends more runes on every cast and hits harder. You pick the size with one button and the element with another, so Fire Blast and Fire Surge are two buttons apart, not two pages of a spellbook.

Bolt · 1 runeBlast · 2 runesWave · 3 runesSurge · 4 runes
FireFire Bolt Magic 1Fire Blast Magic 10Fire Wave Magic 40Fire Surge Magic 70
FrostFrost Bolt Magic 12Frost Blast Magic 12Frost Wave Magic 40Frost Surge Magic 70
StormStorm Bolt Magic 30Storm Blast Magic 30Storm Wave Magic 40Storm Surge Magic 70
ShadowShadow Bolt Magic 50Shadow Blast Magic 50Shadow Wave Magic 50Shadow Surge Magic 70

The level is the first Magic level that spell can be cast at: its element has to be open, and you have to be able to hold a weapon that can load a rune big enough.

The four sizes

SpellRunes a castNeedsBiggest spell ofFirst castableBecauseTo carve them
Bolt1any runeAsh, SootMagic 1Pine wand or staff, the first that can load Ash RunesRunecrafting 1
Blast2Char Runes or betterChar, Cinder, KilnMagic 10Oak wand or staff, the first that can load Char RunesRunecrafting 25
Wave3Forge Runes or betterForge, CrucibleMagic 40Frostwood wand or staff, the first that can load Forge RunesRunecrafting 64
Surge4Starfall Runes or betterStarfall, SunderMagic 70Ancient wand or staff, the first that can load Starfall RunesRunecrafting 88
One rule
The rune decides the biggest spell it can power.A size has no level of its own and no unlock to buy. Load a better rune and the next button lights up. A greyed button says what it is waiting for: Surge needs Starfall Runes or better.
The peg holds
The Magic Power on a rune is what its biggest spell gets.That number is the strength of the arrow of the same tier, as it was. So nothing in section 03 moved: the weapon maths there are a mage casting the biggest spell the rune powers, and the simulator checks the two agree to the digit.
A smaller spell
Spends fewer runes and gets less of the rune.Weapon alone, each size down costs 10.7 to 20% of the damage and saves one rune a cast. The step is bigger early, when the rune is most of the hit, and smaller with good gear.
If you never touch it
You cast the biggest spell your rune powers.That is the default for every save, so a mage who ignores the bar is at full strength. The size and the element can be changed at any time, mid-fight included, and the change applies from the next cast. The last cast of a stack spends what is left.
No gap for the archer to stand in
A rune one tier above the weapon gives its whole strength, as an arrow does.An archer with an Oak bow can load Steel Arrows. A mage with an Oak wand can load Char Runes and cast a Blast with them, which is why Blast starts at Magic 10 and not 20. A level gate on the sizes would leave the mage behind for those ten levels.
The element is the same at every size
A Fire Bolt burns as a Fire Surge does.The burn is a share of the hit and Shadow heals a share of the damage, so both grow with the spell on their own. Frost and Storm do not change.

The last block loads a rune one tier above the staff, which is why it passes melee. An archer who loads Starfall Arrows into an Ancient bow gets the same lift, because the rune and the arrow are the same strength. A wand gives the same shares as a staff to within a point and spends 44% more runes at every size.

What a small spell is for
Making a stack last, not earning more an hour.A stack cast as Bolts lasts up to four times as long and does 1.6 to 2.76 times the damage in total. But hour for hour the biggest spell wins: by 13.3 to 31.9 points for a finished mage, whose runes are nearly free, and a Bolt is never more than 0.9 point ahead even for a new mage who pays full price for every rune.
So the advice is one line
Cast the biggest spell you can feed.Which is what the default does. The smaller sizes are for the day the stack is short, for a mage levelling on runes someone else dropped, and for Sunder Runes.

Worth is from 40 simulated hours each on Goblin Shaman, Ogre Houndmaster, Ashwing Wyvern and Dread Knight, dressed in crafted gear of the tier. On a monster that cannot die the burn is worth 3%; on real ones it resets with every kill and cannot land the killing hit, which is why it measures lower.

One number
Weak is +15%, resisted is -15%.The same 15% the melee types use, so the Monster Log teaches one rule. With Faultline, Fire on a monster that is weak to it measures 117.0% of a plain cast (the 15%, and the burn) and a resisted element 85.0%.
When you pick
Any time. One press, with the fight still running.The spell bar does not lock. A change applies from your next cast. Styles and gear still lock while a fight runs, as they do today. Section 17, question 7.
Fire first
A new mage is never on the wrong element.Nothing below level 19 resists Fire. Frost arrives at Magic 12 with the Goblin Cave, where all five are weak to it; Storm at 30 with the Wolf Den; Shadow at 50, the level of the first Ogre that is weak to it.
No answer everywhere
Fire is right for 21 monsters and wrong for 15.Frost 16 and 12, Storm 13 and 6, Shadow 7 and 7. Every monster is weak to one element, as every monster is weak to one melee type today.

05

Weapons

Two families, every tier from 1 to 11.
FamilyHandsKindCast speedHitCritOther handCasts an hourRole
Wandonelight weapon13% faster than a bladenormal3.4 to 5.8% by tier, the light weapon crit a dagger and a bow already geta buckler, or a shield with the light weapon penalty1,728Fast, and keeps a hand. Rogue. Spends the most runes at any spell size.
Stafftwoheavy weapon25% slower than a blade+44%6.4 to 10.4% by tier, printed on the staffnone1,203The same damage in the same time on 30% fewer runes. Berserker.

A staff hits 44% harder and a wand casts 44% more often: the same damage in the same time, weapon alone. What it gets for the hand it gives up is crit, as a number on the item, because a light weapon already crits and a heavy one does not. On real monsters, dressed, a staff does 98.3 to 99.9% of a wand with the other hand empty. A wand with a buckler in it is ahead of both, and pays for it in runes. No new class: wands are light, staves heavy, and a Guardian can hold a wand and a buckler.

Robes: the third armour class

Ten cloth tiers beside the ten leather tiers, and a third Empyrean set.

Each robe piece is built off the leather piece of the same tier, so the two ladders cannot drift: 62% of its Defence, 50% of its Attack, and in place of crit, dodge and attack speed it carries Magic Power and a chance for a cast to keep its runes. Plate and leather
Every point of Defence on armour that is not cloth costs 0.3% Magic damage, to a limit of 40%.The shield is exempt, as it is for a bow, and a cape is cloth. Measured on a staff, against the same staff in cloth: Lv 40 leather 96.2%, plate 73.4%; Lv 60 leather 86.9%, plate 61.8%; Lv 80 leather 81.3%, plate 55.6%; Lv 99 leather 75.5%, plate 51.0%. You can cast in plate. You will just hit softer, and the number moves as you swap pieces.
In game it says
Cloth · spells at full strength on a robe, -9.6% Magic damage on a Cobalt Chest.Every armour card names its class and what it costs an archer already; it gains one more chip. The Gear tab totals it: Armour that is not cloth: -17% Magic damage.
What you give up
Defence. A mage in cloth has 184 at Lv 99, an archer in leather 217, a fighter in plate with a shield 320.Against a Dread Knight that is 183,919 damage an hour for the mage, 169,752 for the archer and 129,897 for the fighter.
Requirement
Defence, on the same ladder as plate and leather.Recommended for consistency; the alternative is Magic. Question 3.
Also worn by a mage
Bucklers from Cobalt up, Stonewright Gauntlets and every cape with Strength carry Magic Power.The same short list that got Ranged Strength in 0.9.127.2, with the same numbers (1 or 2 on a buckler, 2 on Stonewright, the Strength already on a cape). Stonewright is flagged so it does not weaken spells, as it is flagged light so it does not cost a bow accuracy.

A full cast is the rune's biggest spell, which spends one to four runes. The work is seconds of quarrying, chopping, burning and carving for those runes, from the stone up, the method _rangedecon.js uses for arrows. A batch is 40 runes for each rune the biggest spell spends, so a full cast costs about the same work at every tier and a smaller spell costs a half, a third or a quarter of it. "New" is every skill in the chain at the level the rune unlocks, no tree. "Finished" is 99 with every tree, counting the nodes that save time and not the ones that make a batch bigger, for runes and arrows alike, so both finished prices are the most they can be.

The slot
The quiver slot holds what your weapon spends: arrows, bolts or runes.No thirteenth slot. readyAmmo, ammoFitsWeapon and the tier rule already do the work once they accept a staff: runes carry an ammunition kind of their own, so a bow will not take them and a staff will not take arrows, and the stop message already says which. Question 6.
The fit
A staff or wand casts runes up to its own tier plus one.The bow rule. A tier 7 Ancient Staff casts Starfall Runes, and so a Surge; a Pine Wand does not, at any Magic level. The best staves cast the Sunder Rune.
Keeping the runes
A cast can keep its runes. All of it together stops at 85%, the ceiling arrows already have.Robes 7.5% for five pieces, the Runecrafting tree 50% then 20% then 5%, the Sorcery column 20% and 3%. One roll a cast: it keeps every rune the spell would have spent, or none. Paid as a chance not to spend, exactly as arrow recovery is, so nothing is owed when you retreat or close the game.
Running dry
The fight stops and says why, and you can see it coming.The stop is the block arrows use, widened: You are out of Forge Runes. New for both styles is a readout on your health bar that names the spell and how long the stack lasts at that size: Shadow Wave · 5,520 runes · about 1h 29m, amber under ten minutes. Pick a smaller spell and the time goes up. Section 11.
Away
Offline combat spends runes, and stops when they are gone.It spends nothing for arrows today. One function charges the quiver for the kills the away time earned, at the spell you left it casting, and caps the kills at what the quiver could pay for. The Welcome Back row says how far it got. provisional
Other sources
Anything that casts drops its runes, and the Spire gives Sunder Runes on boss floors.The rule the archers follow for arrows. Section 10.

"With rune cost taken off" can be read two ways, so both are on this page. Leaving the cost out, Magic is 96.1 to 104.8% of melee and of each ranged weapon: section 03. Charging for it, as time, is this table, and nothing that spends ammunition is inside 95 to 105% of melee until it has its saving nodes: a new archer keeps 28.4 to 46.9% of the hour and a finished one 77.8 to 85.7%. That is how Ranged ships.

Runes are priced so a finished mage with a staff keeps 96.1 to 97.3%, inside the band, and a new one keeps 73.8 to 81.7%. A full cast costs 21 to 30% of the work of the arrow of its tier. If it should cost what an arrow costs, it is one number, the batch size, and the finished staff drops to 84.6 to 90.5%. Question 5. A smaller spell cuts the bill further: section 04.

08

Runecrafting: the fifteenth skill

Recommended. Runes, wands, staves, cloth and robes.

Make it a skill. Everything a mage casts and wears comes out of one bench: 79 acts in five tabs. Fletching, which does the same job for an archer, has 69. The other place those acts could go is Crafting, which already has 246.

Precedent
Ranged got Fletching.A bow is a Fletching item made from Woodcutting logs and Smithing heads. A staff is a Runecrafting item made from Woodcutting logs and runes. The two styles read the same way on the skill rail.
Its own loop
Stone from Mining, fuel from Firemaking, silk from the Spider Hollow.One new Mining act quarries Runestone (82% of copper's XP, so it is never the Mining pick). The fuel is what a fire already leaves behind: ash, charcoal and Ember Dust. Charcoal has no use in the game today.
Where rune saving lives
The tree holds 75 of the 85 points of rune saving.Fletching holds arrow recovery the same way. Without a tree the ceiling cannot be reached, and the rune price in section 07 would have to fall to about a fifth to keep a finished mage in the band.
What it costs
A rail row, a banner, a cape, sixteen tree plates and a list of places that count skills.The whole bill is at the end of this section. It is the price of one Fletching.

What Fletching shipped without, so Runecrafting's checklist has it.

From the notes and the audit: XP an hour that froze; a stringing act that was the best XP in the skill; arrows with no source; nothing that fitted the quiver; no cape, so the capstone could not be bought; a level 1 bow that needed level 20 flax; a hardcoded skill count; no achievements; bows gated on Attack; ten tree nodes that did nothing; a combat stat with no save guard. The simulator in this folder asserts the two it can: every input of every act exists in the game, and the tree sums to 98 in Fletching's shape. The rest is the checklist for the build.

Fletching still has no tool, pet or outfit. Runecrafting would ship the same way and they can come later for both.

Spider Silk
The Spider Hollow becomes somewhere you go back to.One Alchemy poultice uses silk today. Every cloth above Linen is silk and one thing from the zone of its tier, so a level 82 mage making Wyrmsilk needs the Wyvern Roost for the glands and about two hundred kills in the Spider Hollow, of things that die in one hit, for the silk. This is the one place the design sends a high-level player to a low zone on purpose. If that is unwelcome, each cloth can take its own zone hide instead: one line a cloth.
Enchanting
Magic takes no Rune Fragments and no Mana Essence.Those are the two reagents an enchant is short of (section 00). Binding every crafted wand and staff once takes 120 Arcane Dust, about 16 minutes of Alchemy for a maxed character. A mage enchants gear at the price everyone pays.

12 of 12 zones have one. The rates are the ones the game already uses for gear on these tables: 0.5% to 1% from a named monster and 3% from the boss, as Wyrmfang, Doomblade and the four hunting-ground bows are today. One that only a named monster drops has the numbers of the crafted weapon of its tier and adds an element it is better with, or an effect, so it is a choice and not a replacement. One the boss also drops sits a little above the crafted tier, where Wyrmfang and Doomblade sit. Their numbers are provisional except where section 14 names them.

Tier follows zone
No early zone drops a late weapon.Every unique is the tier of the unique that zone already drops: tier 3 beside the Warcleaver in the Goblin Cave, tier 7 beside Wyrmfang in the Wyvern Roost, tier 8 beside Doomblade in the Demon Sanctum. Cross-zone scaling is kept: there is nothing to farm in the Rat Warrens past tier 1.
Rare spawns
Four times the chance, never more than 85%.The uniques are ordinary rows on the monster drop table, so rollDrops multiplies them by RARE_DROP_MUL and stops at RARE_DROP_CAP with no new code. A 0.5% staff is 2% from a rare spawn.
Runes from casters
Anything that casts drops its runes, as archers drop arrows.Goblin Shaman: Soot Runes ×8 to 18, 30%. Crypt Wight: Soot Runes ×6 to 14, 22%. Lich (boss): Char Runes ×40 to 80, 60%. Ogre Seer: Kiln Runes ×16 to 36, 30%. Abyssal Fiend: Starfall Runes ×32 to 72, 24%. Sanctum Demon: Starfall Runes ×20 to 48, 14%. The grade is read from the monster level. A top-up, not a supply: a Goblin Shaman kill is worth about four casts.

Combat UI

The prototype, photographed in build 0.9.127.3. Nothing here is a drawing.

Every picture in this section is the real game with the prototype laid over it in memory: the game's own render functions, edited at seven places, drawing a mage. Icons for the new things are flat placeholders, and every placeholder is listed in section 15. The file on disk was never written.

The bar is 649 px wide: a size button is 65 by 46 px and an element button 84 by 46, at 1920 by 1080. A style button in the rail is 29 px tall. The glass under the monster is 229 px tall with the bar in it and reaches 23 px up the monster's picture, which is the empty margin under its feet. The second draft had these buttons in the Training panel in the right-hand rail. That rail is 573 px tall and in a raid it also carries Momentum and the three abilities: the old layout would have needed 693 px there. That is why they moved. The buttons act on the press, not the release: the combat panel is rebuilt on every kill, and a click that straddles a kill would lose its target.

Not drawn
A cast effect on the monster.The damage numbers carry the element. A flash on the monster in the element's colour would reuse the hit flash the arena has; no new art. provisional
Plain words
Every string on these screens, as it would ship.Fire: A hit can set the monster on fire. It burns for 8 seconds. Frost: A hit can chill the monster. It attacks 25% slower for 6 seconds. Storm: 4% of casts cannot miss. Shadow: You heal for 3% of the damage you deal. Wave: 3 runes a cast, +15 Magic Power Surge needs Starfall Runes or better. Shadow Wave hits the Ogre Houndmaster for 198. Cloth · spells at full strength 1.5% of casts keep their runes 25% slower attacks
Bows get it too
The loaded count and time on the health bar works for arrows.It is one function that reads the quiver. An archer has no such readout today.
12

Everything it plugs into

One line each. Every one of these reads a weapon, a damage stat or a combat level.
Combat Mastery
A fifth column, Sorcery: 30 points, and a 4 point bridge to Warfare. Magic levels pay for all 34.One point at every third Magic level and a second at 99. The board goes from 132 to 166 and what can be earned rises by the same 34, so the audit's rule that the two match still holds. The tree key is sorc, because magic is Warfare. Any-weapon nodes follow the staff through the _dk gate, which gets a third branch. Nodes are below.
Enchants
A new stat, Magic damage ("of the Seer"), and a staff pool.The same base numbers as the Attack and Ranged damage enchants (0.005 on gear and 0.02 on jewellery, before tier and roll). Staves and wands roll from Magic damage, crit chance, crit damage and lifesteal, and the unique enchant on one is Magic damage. Head and hands gain it as a sixth stat and jewellery as an eighth, so every other roll in those two pools gets a little rarer, as it did when Ranged damage went in. Three key lists in combatEnchantBonuses drop a stat they do not know in silence.
Gems
Wyrdstone: +2, +4, +8% Magic damage.The twin of Hawkseye. Two key lists in combatSocketBonuses. Sanguine gems, which are damage with any weapon, follow the staff with no change.
Potions and food
Arcane Draught I: +2 Magic Power for 2 minutes, Alchemy 45. Arcane Draught II: +4 Magic Power for 3 minutes, Alchemy 78.The twin of the Hawkeye pair, from Nightbloom ×3, which Farming grows from level 40. Warrior's Triple Brew gains +3 Magic Power beside its other stats. A potion stat has to be in seven key lists to work and five more places to be seen; the Hawkeye Draught is missing from those five today. Strength from a potion or food does not reach a spell. It does reach a bow, as a stated exception: question 14 asks whether Magic should have the same one.
Capes
Every cape with Strength carries the same Magic Power.As they carry Ranged Strength. The Runecrafter's Cape is the fifteenth skill cape and its tree node doubles a batch of runes.
Sets
Dawnveil, four pieces: +10% crit chance and +8% damage.The third Empyrean set, beside Dawnward and Sunweave. Set bonuses that are damage with any weapon follow the staff. The Iron Legion title bonus that says melee stays melee.
Raids
Rally, Ruin and Brace work as they are. The spell bar stays live.Ruin multiplies whatever you hit with. Styles and gear lock while a fight is active and a raid runs as one fight, so a fighter keeps one damage type for the run. A mage does not have to: with the bar live, one who watches can match each stage. Left alone, each raid has an element that is right for about half of it: Sunken Barrow: Storm, 3 of 6 stages; Emberforge Deep: Frost, 4 of 6 stages; Abyssal Throne: Fire, 3 of 7 stages; Empyrean Throne: Shadow, 5 of 8 stages. Question 7.
Momentum
A staff charges the three abilities about 30% slower than a wand.Momentum is 7 for every hit that lands and a staff lands fewer, harder hits. Any slow weapon has this handicap today. Question 11.
Spire and Ascension
Ascension raises Magic Power on a piece with its other numbers.One line in gearStats, beside Ranged Strength. The per-rank bonuses are crit, lifesteal and health, so nothing is added. A floor that borrows a zone or raid monster copies its elements with its weakness. Section 14 has the wall.
Slayer
Nothing.Tasks count kills by family, whatever killed them.
Guilds
A seat for Runecrafting, and a requirement check that knows about Magic.gdReqMet sends only the four melee stat names to a combat level, so a quest that asks for a Ranged or Magic level cannot be met. One line, and it fixes Ranged too.
Achievements and Steam
Six proposed: Magic 99, Runecrafting 99, a kill with each element in one zone, a full set of robes, a raid cleared with a staff, the Spire to floor 30 with a staff.Each is a row in the Steam schema and an icon, and the schema upload is its own step. "Full Board" would need Magic 99 once the board has a fifth column: question 8. provisional
Offline combat
Spends runes while you are away, and stops when they are gone.offlineCombatResolve has no ammunition in it, so a bow is free offline today. One function: charge the quiver for the kills the time away earned, at the spell you left it casting, less what was kept, and cap the kills at what the quiver could pay for. The weakness is counted; the four element effects are not, to keep the offline sum simple. Question 10. provisional
The demo
Capped with no new code.The level 10 cap is one generic line in grantCombatXp, so a new combat stat is capped the day it exists, and skills are capped the same way. A demo player gets Ash Runes, a Pine Wand and Staff, Linen robes and Fire. All ten monsters in the two demo zones are weak to Fire. Frost is the first thing the full game adds, at Magic 12.
Classes
No new class.A wand is a light weapon, so it is the Rogue weapon and gets the light weapon crit. A staff is heavy, so it is the Berserker weapon. A Guardian holds a wand and a buckler, or a full shield with the penalty a dagger already takes.
Compendium and satchel
Nothing new to build.New items appear when first held, as now. Runes sort with arrows, cloth with materials, robes, wands and staves with gear.
Wiki
The tables are automatic. An Elements page is new._wikigen.js walks the skill and stat lists. The monster pages need a weak element and a resisted one beside the damage type.
Main menu
The save slot shows the wrong combat level for anything but melee.mmSummary averages the four melee stats. It should call combatLevel(). A Ranged gap, fixed in passing.
Effects bar
A line for Magic Power, and the one Ranged Strength never got.The bar and the status chips list each potion stat by name and know neither.

Three near misses
Worth knowing before the build.magic is taken twice: it is the Warfare tree key and the stat name, which is why the column is sorc. _rune already ends one id, Drakeforged Rune, a raid material, so runes are recognised by their ammunition kind and never by name. cloth appears 19 times as a colour key inside icon palettes; no item carries it, so it is free as an armour flag.

Balance, measured

52 checks, 0 failing. Run it yourself: node _magedesign/sim.js

The simulator boots the real game, lays the prototype over it and asks the game's own functions for every number: playerAccuracy, playerMaxHit, playerSwingMs, actMs, spireScale, the enchant, gem, Mastery and Ascension code. The sword, shortbow, longbow and crossbow columns reproduce _rangedsim.js, _rangedstr.js and _wall.js to the digit, because those weapons run through functions the prototype does not touch. Sections 03, 04, 07 and 08 have the weapon, spell, rune and skill tables. The rest is here.

The file

16

Build order

Nine slices. Each ships on its own and leaves the game whole.
01

The rules nobody sees

The Magic stat, the combat level formula, the save guards, Magic damage and Magic Power through every place that sums a stat, and the demo cap. Nothing can be equipped yet, so nothing on screen changes. The simulator in this folder becomes _magesim.js and joins the four harnesses, with the "no save moves" assertion first.

no art
no visible change
02

A wand, a rune and Fire

The playable core. Runecrafting as a whole skill (it cannot ship without its 98 point tree, rail row and cape): Quarry runestone, eight runes, seven wands, seven staves. Casting: the three styles, the four spell sizes, the runes spent on every cast, the stop when they run out, the fit rule, the spell bar under the health bar, the Magic line under Training, the loaded count on the health bar for runes and arrows, the item cards, the Magic loadout tile, and the Magic damage enchant with its staff pool, so a staff can never roll Attack. One element, Fire, always on: Fire Bolt to Fire Surge. This slice alone is a complete third way to fight.

42 icons, about 199 KB
the ceiling moves here

Frost, Storm and Shadow, the four buttons, and the pass over every monster, raid stage and Spire monster. The chips on the monster card, the two tags in the Monster Log, the colour on damage numbers. This is the slice that makes Magic its own thing, and the one to cut if the identity is wrong.

17

What I need you to decide

Every open call, with what I would do and what changes if you say no.
1. Is this the identity: four elements, chosen between fights?It is the only part of the design that is not Ranged with a different icon, and it costs a monster pass and four buttons.Recommended: yes.If no: slice 3 is not built and Magic ships with one damage type. Without Fire it sits at 96.3 to 97.1% of melee, so the wand cast speed moves from 0.87 to 0.85 to give the 3% back. Section 04 and the Monster Log tags go.
2. Is Runecrafting a fifteenth skill?79 acts, a 98 point tree, a cape, a rail row and a banner.Recommended: yes.If no: runes and robes become Crafting tabs (246 acts becomes 311) and wands and staves become Fletching tabs. There is no tree, so rune saving tops out near 30% and the batch has to grow from 40 to about 185 to keep a finished mage where section 07 has it. Nineteen icons and the bill in section 08 are saved.
3. Do robes need Defence or Magic?All armour needs Defence today.Recommended: Defence. One rule, and the Warded style has a reason to exist.If no: robes gate on Magic, a pure mage wears the best cloth with Defence 1, and Warded is the style nobody picks. Nothing else moves.
4. What should casting in plate cost?As designed: 0.3% damage for each point of Defence that is not cloth, to 40%. Full plate is about half damage at level 99.Recommended: as designed. It is the one number that makes robes matter.If no: a softer slope (0.2%) lets a mage wear leather for nearly nothing, and robes are then only worth their rune saving. A harder one makes plate useless rather than expensive.
5. What should a rune cost against an arrow?As designed a full-size cast costs 21 to 30% of the work of the arrow of its tier, which is what keeps a finished mage with a staff inside 95 to 105% of melee with the cost taken off. A finished archer is at 77.8 to 85.7%.Recommended: as designed, because you asked for the band to hold with the cost taken off.If no: at the arrow's price the batch drops from 40 to about 10 and a finished staff is 84.6 to 90.5%. Magic and Ranged then cost the same to feed, and neither is in the band.
6. Do runes share the quiver slot?One slot holds whatever your weapon spends.Recommended: yes. No thirteenth slot on the doll and no change to saved loadouts.If no: a rune pouch of its own means a bow and a staff can both stay loaded when you swap, at the cost of a new slot in the doll, the loadout format and every list of body slots.
7. Can the spell change during a fight?The first two drafts locked the size and the element with the style buttons. You asked for the spell to be easy to pick in combat.Decided: yes. The spell bar works while the fight runs and a change applies from the next cast.Still open: raids and the Spire. Gear and style lock mid-fight today, so a fighter keeps one damage type for a whole raid and hits the weakness on about half of its stages (3 of 6, 4 of 6, 4 of 7, 3 of 8). A mage who leaves the bar alone gets the same half. One who watches it can hit the weakness on every stage, which is worth about 7% over a run. I have left it live, because that is what you asked for and raids are the part of the game that already rewards watching. If it should not be so, the bar locks in a raid and on the Spire only: one condition.
8. Where do the 34 Sorcery points come from?From Magic levels: one every third level and a second at 99. The board can then only be filled by a character with Magic 99.Recommended: Magic levels. It keeps the board exactly fillable and gives a non-mage a reason to cast.If no: the points need another source, such as more Spire floors, or the column shrinks. "Full Board" stays reachable without Magic.
9. How should five Mastery columns fit?The board needs 1702 px and the panel shows 1366. The mock-up is drawn at 80%.Recommended: draw it smaller, as mocked, and look at it before deciding. It is the one mock-up I am not sure reads well.If no: it scrolls sideways, which it can do today, and the new column starts off-screen. Or the gutters narrow and all five fit at full size, which needs a layout pass.

How this was made. Four scripts in _magedesign/. sim.js boots build 0.9.127.3 in jsdom as the desktop game, lays design.js and overlay.js over it, and writes every number on this page to results.json. shoot.js does the same in headless Chrome with ui.js on top and photographs it. names.js reads display names and what each material is used for today. build.js prints this page from all of it, and refuses to write it if a number comes out missing. Change a number in design.js, run the four, and the page and its pictures follow.

What was not touched. cindervale.html was read and never written. The build was not bumped. Nothing was committed or pushed. No art was made.

Measured 2026-10-08 against build 0.9.127.3, 12,507,965 bytes.
